label: Demo Stream Resync Hold
description: Keeps a live demo stream decodable after a resync. When the engine forces a full snapshot for a streamed player (relay reconnect, lost blocks, periodic keyframe), this plugin keeps forcing full snapshots for that player on the following server frames until the client acknowledges one of them, or the cap runs out. Without it the snapshots right behind a single full one are deltas from messages the relay never received, and the relay's picture can stop until the next keyframe. Off by default: it was measured on a duel server only (two streamed players), not yet on a populated server or in team modes. Cost: one to three extra full snapshots (about 250 bytes each in a duel) per resync and per keyframe interval for each streamed player; never more holds at once than Max holds at once, and none while the relay is behind. For a periodic keyframe the plugin cannot see which player the engine meant and works it out from its own record of each player's last full snapshot. With sv_demoStreamKeyframeSec 0 there are no keyframe holds, but a relay reconnect and lost blocks are still repaired, the first player after a reconnect included. A hold that has waited more than 60 server frames for its turn is dropped, unless it repairs a real loss. Does nothing when the demo stream itself (sv_demoStream) is off. Console: qlx !resynchold prints the counters. Requires the minqlxtended fork build with the live demo stream (runtime-source addon).

commands.name: resynchold
commands.description: Prints whether the hold is on, the limits and the counters: holds started, ended by acknowledgement, ended by the cap, cancelled, full snapshots forced, holds started for a keyframe and how many of those were a guess, waiting holds that were dropped, and holds and forced snapshots per player slot. With log: the last hold starts, hold ends and relay link changes with their times (64 on the console, 10 in chat).

cvars.label: Enabled
cvars.description: Turns the hold on. Off: the plugin forces nothing and does not query the engine. Read about once a second, so a change applies without a restart.

cvars.label: Max hold (full snapshots)
cvars.description: Most full snapshots one hold may force, one per server frame. 8 frames are 200 ms at sv_fps 40. A hold normally ends earlier, as soon as the client acknowledges a forced snapshot; a player with a higher round trip than the cap covers is not fully repaired until the next keyframe.

cvars.label: Max holds at once
cvars.description: Most holds that run at the same time, which is also the most full snapshots the plugin forces in one server frame for all players together. Further holds wait their turn.
